goal: Plan a framework, language runtime or major-version migration across a large codebase using Recursive Languag…
use: Plan a framework, language runtime or major-version migration across a large codebase using Recursive Language Model (RLM) decomposition, with an inventory of affected code, risks, phased steps and rollback. Use when asked to migrate, upgrade a major version, or replace a library, on code too large to read in one pass.

steps.note: Define the migration. Ask the user for the source and target: for example, "React 17 to 18", "Python 3.9 to 3.12", "Express to Fastify".
Map. For each chunk, run a fresh sub-task (a subagent if you can start one) that sees the chunk and the "Chunk task" below.

protocol.title: Define the migration
protocol.text: Ask the user for the source and target: for example, "React 17 to 18", "Python 3.9 to 3.12", "Express to Fastify". Ask what must not change, such as public API or database schema. Do not start without these.

protocol.title: Inspect
protocol.text: Run `python3 <skill>/scripts/rlm_corpus.py scan <repo>`. Agree the scope if the code base is very large, then narrow it with `--include`.

protocol.title: Graph
protocol.text: Run `python3 <skill>/scripts/rlm_corpus.py graph <repo>`. Use it to order the work: leaf modules first, then the modules that depend on them.

protocol.title: Map
protocol.text: For each chunk, run a fresh sub-task (a subagent if you can start one) that sees the chunk and the "Chunk task" below. If you cannot start sub-tasks, run `python3 <skill>/scripts/rlm_corpus.py pending "$WORK/chunks" "$WORK/out"` and process the first listed chunk, then run `pending` again until nothing is pending.

protocol.title: Verify
protocol.text: Open each cited file and line, confirm each finding against the source, and drop any finding you cannot confirm.

protocol.title: Plan
protocol.text: Write the plan in the format below.

protocol.title: Clean up
protocol.text: Delete `$WORK` after the plan is delivered.
